_provenance: Every cell is a plain-form decision measured against a real PMS: kids (1.43.4) and zen (1.42.2) read-only over 24 rows chosen for their containers, codecs, channel counts, bit depths and subtitle kinds, and plexscratch (1.43.4) over one row MADE for the model -- two audio tracks that carry no language at all, muxed into its writable media directory with ffmpeg, scanned, and read back. `rows` holds each row's Media as the reference wrote it; `cells` holds what each of the 78 client profiles answered for it. The plexscratch row is recorded in BOTH of its states: `selected`, after a client has chosen a track with `PUT /library/parts/{id}?audioStreamID=`, and `pre-selection`, after `audioStreamID=-1` clears that -- the item's Stream rows are byte-identical in the two and 41 of the 78 answers are not. plexsim holds a chosen track, so `selected` is the state the model reproduces and `pre-selection` is recorded and not emulated. zen's row 19813 has the same shape -- two audio tracks naming no language -- and answers 68 of the 78 identically to the made row's `pre-selection` state, the other ten being its selected sidecar subtitle refusing earlier; it is recorded in that state for the same reason. Cycle 35 added zen's row 3831, a 4.6 GB mp4 whose h264 is `high 10` at 10 bits with 64-bit offsets: it is the corpus's only row that trips a `list=` limitation (Android's `video.profile`), its only `has64bitOffsets` true, and the witness for the ` [list]` suffix a `list=` refusal carries.
